definition: Robot Operating System (ROS or ros) is an open-source robotics middleware suite.
details: Although ROS is not an operating system (OS) but a set of software frameworks for robot software development, it provides services designed for a heterogeneous computer cluster such as hardware abstraction, low-level device control, implementation of commonly used functionality, message-passing between processes, and package management. Running sets of ROS-based processes are represented in a graph architecture where processing takes place in nodes that may receive, post, and multiplex sensor data, control, state, planning, actuator, and other messages.

explainer.lead: ROS is a middleware suite that supplies the plumbing for robot software: hardware abstraction, device control, message passing and package management. It matters because it lets teams reuse common functionality instead of rebuilding it for every robot.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as a shared toolkit and messenger service for robots: each part of the robot does its job and passes notes to the others through a common post office.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers split robot behaviour into nodes that receive, post and multiplex sensor data across a processing graph. A pitfall is treating it as an actual operating system; it is a framework running on a heterogeneous computer cluster.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, ROS is not an operating system but a set of software frameworks providing hardware abstraction, low-level device control, message passing and package management over a graph of nodes. Its scope is robot software development, not kernel-level OS functions.

explainer.example: A wheel-controller node publishes odometry while a sensor node posts range readings, and a planning node subscribes to both and issues velocity commands.
